company.name: Tenneco Clean Air India Ltd

profile.what: Indian arm of US-based Tenneco (owned by funds managed or advised by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, AR FY26). Makes exhaust and after-treatment systems (hot end: catalytic converters, DPF/SCR; cold end: mufflers, pipes), powertrain parts (spark plugs, ignition coils, engine bearings, sealings, heat shields) and ride-control products (shock absorbers, struts, DCx DaVinci and semi-active suspension) for Indian car, truck, tractor and off-highway makers, plus a small aftermarket and export business.
profile.marketShare: FY26 value share (CRISIL): CV clean air 58% (#1), off-highway clean air 68% (#1), PV shock absorbers and struts 55% (#1); PV clean air ~20% (Motilal Oswal); engine bearings #2 (CV 34%, PV 44%, FY25).
profile.customersMix: No customer above 22% of VAR; top customer 19.9%, customers 2-5 42.4%, 6-10 16.7% (FY26). Serves all top-7 PV and top-5 CV OEMs; not present in clean air at India's largest (Japanese) PV maker until a CAFE-3 programme expected around FY28-29.

history.event: Tenneco Clean Air India Pvt Ltd incorporated (Tamil Nadu). The Federal-Mogul India ignition, bearings and sealings companies were fellow subsidiaries in the Tenneco group.

Ownership chain (AR FY26): immediate parent Tenneco Mauritius Holdings; ultimate parent Tenneco LLC (Delaware), owned through holding entities by AP IX Pegasus Holdings L.P., i.e. funds managed or advised by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.

Tenneco Automotive India sells Motocare India (aftermarket distribution) to a fellow subsidiary for Rs829 cr; the gain sits in capital reserve on consolidation, the cash was collected in FY26 and paid out as dividends.

Common-control combination: the company acquires Tenneco Automotive India and the three Federal-Mogul India companies (ignition, sealings, bearings) by share swap (189.5 mn new shares); pooled and restated from 1-Apr-2022.
Four interim dividends to Tenneco before the IPO: Rs25.68 a share, Rs1,036.6 cr in total.
Listed on NSE/BSE after a Rs3,600 cr IPO, a pure offer for sale by Tenneco Mauritius Holdings at Rs397 (9.07 cr shares; promoter 97.25% to 74.79%); opened at Rs505 on NSE.
Q3FY26: Rs20.3 cr (post-tax) one-off for the new labour codes (gratuity definition, effective 21-Nov-2025); Kharkhoda (Haryana) Clean Air greenfield announced (Rs71 cr).
Q4FY26: lifetime order book Rs12,400 cr (Mar-2026); western-India ART plant announced (Rs69 cr).
Promoter block sale (floor Rs515; ~Rs525-529 traded; 90-day lock-up on further sales); 9.1 cr shares traded on NSE that day. Reported total sale 6.05 cr shares (15.0% of equity).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Tenneco Clean Air India (consolidated; Rs crore). Two reported segments measured on value-added revenue (VAR = revenue less pass-through substrates): Clean Air & Powertrain Solutions (CA&PT) and Advanced Ride Technologies (ART). The engine models one revenue line; the segment build (CA&PT VAR + ART VAR + substrates = revenue) is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue in TENNIND.ctx.js. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Revenue = VAR + substrates. VAR: CA&PT +11% / +14% / +13% and ART +22% / +16% / +15% (lineBuild). FY27: Q1FY27 VAR +18.4% (CA&PT +9.6%, ART +27.9%) on the post-GST-cut PV boom; ART runs above 90% utilisation, so H2 growth slows against Q3-Q4FY26 bases that already grew 24-26%. FY28-29: the Rs12,400 cr lifetime order book covers more than 100% of the FY28 revenue target (company, Mar-2026); CAFE-3 (expected from 2027) and Kharkhoda (Clean Air, SoP ~Q3FY27) and the western ART plant lift CA&PT; DaVinci DCx and semi-active dampers keep ART ahead of PV production. Substrates (precious-metal coated, passed through at cost) held at ~11% of VAR (Q1FY27 11.8%, FY26 9.9%).

lineBuild._why: Company disclosure (Q4FY26 call, 3-Jun-2026): FY26 VAR Rs4,918 cr = CA&PT Rs2,430 cr + ART Rs2,489 cr; revenue from operations Rs5,404 cr, so substrates Rs486 cr. Forecast VAR by segment below; substrates are the balance to model revenue and must stay within 9-13% of VAR (ctx check).

assumptions._marginWhy: On revenue (Screener basis). FY26 17.1% of revenue = 18.8% of VAR (highest ever); Q1FY27 16.0% of revenue = 17.9% of VAR, down 170 bp YoY on non-indexed commodity costs (crude-linked rubber, plastics after the West Asia war), rupee weakness and the running cost of a listed company. Mix works against the margin: in FY25 CA&PT earned 23.8% of VAR and ART 12.8% (RHP via JM Financial), and ART is the faster-growing half (53-54% of VAR by FY28-29E vs 47% in FY25); at FY26 segment margins the mix alone takes ~0.2-0.3 points a year off. FY27E 18.0% of VAR: steel is indexed with a one-quarter lag and recoveries are under negotiation (CFO, Aug-2026). FY28-29E 18.6-18.8% of VAR as listing costs are absorbed (CFO, Dec-2025: margins 'come back to the same levels') and DCx/export mix helps (export margins 'in line or better'). Royalty (2.5% of revenue net of intercompany sales) and network service fees stay inside costs.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance Rs350-450 cr ('indicative', fully from internal accruals, Q1FY27 call), including Rs140 cr for the two announced plants (Kharkhoda Clean Air Rs71 cr; western India ART Rs69 cr). We take the low end because FY26 cash capex was only Rs115 cr and H1 spend had not been disclosed by 30-Sep. Rs280 cr a year in FY28-29 for semi-active suspension, CAFE-3/BS-VII hot ends and export-transfer lines.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs108 cr = 9.0% of average gross block (Rs1,195 cr; Screener schedules). Q1FY27 Rs28 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP flat), so 9% on a growing block front-loads depreciation.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening net cash (Mar-2026: cash Rs571 cr less Rs51 cr of lease liabilities = Rs520 cr). Bank deposits ~6.5%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury items (export incentives, scrap/asset-sale gains, interest on deposits with landlords). FY26 other income Rs59 cr before the Rs27 cr labour-code exceptional (AR FY26), but Q1FY26 carried a one-off from the Motocare disposal and other one-off income (CFO, Aug-2026; Q1FY26 Rs31 cr); the last three quarters ran at Rs9-12 cr a quarter before exceptional items. FY27E = Rs34 cr treasury + Rs6 cr = Rs40 cr, in line with the ~Rs37 cr TTM run rate.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 finance cost Rs34 cr (Q1FY27 Rs8 cr): lease interest plus interest on other items (AR FY26: Rs24 cr 'interest on others'); no bank debt.
assumptions._taxWhy: New regime 25.17% plus non-deductible items; FY25 24.5%, FY26 25.9% (incl. exceptional), Q1FY27 25%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: All FY26 dividends (Rs1,037 cr, Rs25.68 a share) were paid to Tenneco before the IPO (Apr-Aug 2025); the Board recommended no final dividend for FY26, citing capacity expansion, technology and 'other business opportunities' (AR FY26), and management talked of M&A options for surplus cash (Aug-2026). No interim declared by 30-Sep, so FY27E 0%; we assume a policy payout of 25-30% from FY28E (our assumption, not guidance).

dcf._betaWhy: Tied to Indian truck, tractor and car production (cyclical) but net cash and diversified across PV/CV/off-highway: beta 0.95, cost of equity 12.2%. No debt, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian vehicle production ~5-6% plus emission and ride content; but clean-air content disappears in battery EVs: 6%, the top of the house range only because ART is powertrain-agnostic.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~14% in FY29E to 8%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 16.5% of revenue (~18.3% of VAR): exhaust content shrinks as EV share rises.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~3.5% of revenue long run (FY23-26 1.2-2.1%, FY27E 5.5%); depreciation ~2.2% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: PV and truck production keep growing near double digits; DCx becomes standard in A/B-segment cars; CAFE-3 and BS-VII arrive on time; exports rise towards 20% of VAR (JM Financial's FY30 view) at better margins; VAR margin back above 19%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Post-GST demand fades and CVs turn down; BS-VII is watered down and CAFE-3 delayed; commodity costs are not recovered; the parent raises its charges or moves export programmes elsewhere; VAR margin stuck near 17%.

cover.headline: India's exhaust and shock-absorber leader: ride control carries the growth, the parent carries the risk
cover.lead: Tenneco Clean Air India makes exhaust and after-treatment systems, spark plugs and bearings (49% of value-added revenue, VAR) and shock absorbers and struts (51%) for Indian car, truck and tractor makers; it leads in truck exhaust (58% share), off-highway exhaust (68%) and car shock absorbers (55%). It listed on 19-Nov-2025 through a ₹3,600 cr sale of shares by its US parent at ₹397. VAR grew 12.3% in FY26 and 18.4% in Q1FY27, but almost all of the growth is ride control (+28% in Q1); exhaust grew 9.6% against a 16% market, and the margin slipped to 17.9% of VAR. We forecast EPS of ₹16.78 / ₹20.30 / ₹23.87 for FY27-29E, below the street. The street values the stock on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (JM Financial 29x FY28E, Motilal Oswal 30x Sep-28E). The house rule (its own forward P/E median since listing, 29.0x, adjusted by the auto-component peers' −4.0% move over the same ten months) gives **28x Sep-28E EPS of ₹22.09 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹549, DCF ₹517, both close to the price. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Ride control is the growth engine, and it does not care about EVs
arguments.p: ART VAR grew 19.7% in FY26 and 27.9% in Q1FY27 (₹719 cr), with plants above 90% utilised. DCx DaVinci (a mechanical "passive-plus" damper at about twice the content of a conventional one) has moved from one launch customer to four new customers in a quarter, and a smaller DCx32 targets A/B-segment cars. Every car needs dampers, electric or not. We model ART VAR +{{as.lineBuild.artGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.lineBuild.artGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.lineBuild.artGrowth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: Exhaust is a regulation business that is lagging its market until FY28
arguments.p: CA&PT grew 5.5% in FY26 and 9.6% in Q1FY27 while its served market grew 16%: it has no content in battery EVs and no clean-air business at India's largest car maker, whose sales jumped after the GST cut. Entry there comes with CAFE-3 (expected FY28-29); CAFE-3 and BS-VII add ₹1,300-1,400 cr of industry content. Until then we model +{{as.lineBuild.caGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.lineBuild.caGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.lineBuild.caGrowth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: The parent is both the moat and the toll
arguments.p: Tenneco supplies the technology (thousands of patents, Euro VII work, semi-active suspension) and ~70% of the export order book. In return it takes a 2.5% royalty on revenue including pass-through substrates plus network fees: ₹142 cr in FY26, 2.6% of revenue and 15% of EBITDA. It took ₹1,037 cr of dividends before the IPO, sold 22% at the IPO and another 15% in August 2026; a 90-day lock-up ends around mid-November.

arguments.h: Valuation: a fair price for the history, a discount to the street
arguments.p: At ₹508.25 the stock trades at 25.0x our FY28E and 23.0x Sep-28E EPS against a 29.0x forward median since listing (range 24.7-35.3x). Our 28x sits just below the street's 29-30x; the target is below the street's median (₹667) because our EPS is lower (FY28E ₹20.30 vs JM's ₹23.3). The DCF (₹517) and EV/EBITDA (₹549) only support today's price: the upside rests on the P/E holding.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the half-yearly order book (domestic and export split), H1 capex and whether non-indexed cost increases were recovered.
End of the parent's 90-day lock-up (around mid-November 2026): Tenneco no longer needs to sell for minimum public shareholding, but any further sale is an overhang.
CAFE-3 for cars (expected from 2027; management: "mid of 2027") and the BS-VII notification: content per vehicle and the entry into India's largest car maker.
Kharkhoda Clean Air plant (start of production ~Q3FY27 per JM Financial) and the western-India ride-control plant.
Value of the spark-plug order from a large PV maker (not yet disclosed) and any acquisition (management: "wait for the right time").

sections.title: Two businesses under one roof: exhaust and powertrain parts (49%), shock absorbers and struts (51%)

blocks.p: Tenneco Clean Air India is the Indian arm of Tenneco, a US auto-parts maker owned by funds managed or advised by affiliates of Apollo Global Management. It has 12 plants (Chakan I and II, Chennai, Pondicherry, Sanand, Pithampur, Bawal, Bhiwadi, Parwanoo, Hosur, Pune) and two technical centres, and sells to 119 customers. In FY26 it had revenue of ₹5,404 cr and value-added revenue (VAR: revenue less substrates passed through at cost) of ₹4,918 cr.

blocks.p: Domestic sales were 93.6% of FY26 VAR and exports 5.9% (about 7% of revenue in Q1FY27). Capacity: 3 mn cold ends (51% used in FY26), 2 mn hot ends (78%) and 21 mn shock absorbers and struts (90%). Management says CA&PT runs above 80% and ART above 90% after the GST-cut demand jump, which is why two greenfields were announced: Kharkhoda, Haryana (Clean Air, ₹71 cr) and western India (ride control, ₹69 cr).

blocks.callout: **How it makes money:** it designs (with Tenneco's global technology) and assembles systems that are validated for a vehicle platform and then supplied for its 5-7 year life. Steel and substrates are passed through (steel with a quarter's lag; substrates at cost), so profit is earned on conversion and engineering. That is why management reports margins on VAR and why reported revenue can fall while profit rises (FY25).

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** the listed company is a 2025 construction. Its history before FY23 cannot be compared, its FY26 cash flow is flattered by an intra-group sale, and its pre-IPO dividends were set by the parent. That is not wrong, but it means the track record a minority investor can judge is only three-and-a-half years long.

sections.title: Content grows with emission law and with car buyers' taste for SUVs; volume follows the vehicle cycle

blocks.p: Exhaust after-treatment content is set by emission law: BS-VI (Apr-2020) multiplied content per vehicle; BS-VI stage 2 (RDE) followed in 2023. Next: CAFE-3 fuel-economy norms for cars expected in 2027 (gasoline direct injection needs particulate filters from 2027, per management), TREM-V for tractors and BS-VII (not notified by 30-Sep-2026). Management sizes CAFE-3 + BS-VII at ₹1,300-1,400 cr of extra industry content. JM Financial (Jan-2026): PV clean-air market ₹4,650-5,100 cr by FY30 (6-8% CAGR), CV/off-highway 13-15% CAGR; CAFE adds ₹1,000-1,500 per car, BS-VII ~₹2,000 per truck.

Shock absorbers and struts go into every vehicle, ICE or electric. Premiumisation (UVs 34.6% of PV volume in FY20, 65.4% in FY25, JM Financial) and EVs (heavier, low centre of gravity) push buyers towards passive-plus (DCx, ~2x conventional content) and semi-active (~4x) dampers. Domestic PV OE suspension market +8-10% CAGR FY25-30 (CRISIL via JM).

Served market (PV+CV, company) grew 16.2% in Q1FY27 on the Sep-2025 GST cut for small cars and a CV upcycle; the West Asia war lifted crude-linked input costs from Mar-2026. Battery EVs carry no exhaust: about 20% of VAR (PV clean air) is exposed to full EV adoption (JM Financial); hybrids, CNG and flex-fuel keep or raise content.

sections.title: Ride control grows twice as fast; exhaust earns almost twice the margin

blocks.h: Advanced Ride Technologies (51% of FY26 VAR)

blocks.p: ART VAR rose from ₹2,079 cr in FY25 to ₹2,489 cr in FY26 (+19.7%) and ₹719 cr in Q1FY27 (+27.9%). Tenneco has 55% of the Indian car shock-absorber and strut market (52% a year earlier). The growth comes from three things: more cars (the GST cut helped small cars most), richer products (DCx DaVinci, launched with a leading Indian PV maker in Q3FY26, now on several programmes; semi-active electronic dampers on Mahindra's BE6 and XEV 9e) and new customers (four in Q1FY27, new even for conventional dampers). Plants run above 90%; a ₹69 cr western-India plant is coming. The weak spot is margin: in FY25 ART earned only 12.8% of VAR against 23.8% in CA&PT (RHP data shown by JM Financial).

CA&PT VAR was ₹2,303 cr in FY25 and ₹2,430 cr in FY26 (+5.5%); Q1FY27 ₹663 cr (+9.6%). It includes exhaust after-treatment (58% of truck and 68% of off-highway clean air), spark plugs and ignition, bearings and sealings. CA&PT grew 9.6% against a 16% served market: no exhaust content in EVs (~3-3.5 points) and no presence at the leading Japanese PV OEM, which grew strongly after the GST cut; like-for-like market ~8-10%. New wins: a spark-plug order at a large car maker, PV hot-end and CNG cold-end programmes, an SCV after-treatment system, a heat-shield order from Tenneco America, and the first clean-air programme at the Japanese PV leader (for CAFE-3, 2028-29). Kharkhoda (₹71 cr) adds capacity in the north.

blocks.p: EBITDA on VAR rose from 14.6% (FY23) and 14.3% (FY24) to 18.6% (FY25) and 18.8% (FY26), helped by Tenneco's P3 cost programme, better plant loading and price recoveries. It fell to 17.9% in Q1FY27 (19.6% a year earlier). Management gave two reasons: the cost of being a listed company (a full leadership team, directors' fees, compliance, legal and IT) and inputs that are not indexed to customer prices (crude-linked plastics and rubber, LPG/CNG) after the West Asia war. Steel is indexed back-to-back with a one-quarter lag. Recoveries and productivity added 60 bp in Q1. Employee cost rose 30% YoY in Q4FY26 (JM Financial).

sections.title: Tenneco takes 2.6% of revenue in fees: fair for the technology, but it charges royalty on pass-through substrates

blocks.p: Tenneco India pays its parent group a royalty for technology and trademarks and, from FY26, "network fees" that replaced management-support and corporate-support charges. FY26: royalty ₹119.2 cr, network fees ₹22.8 cr, total ₹142 cr (2.6% of revenue, 15.4% of EBITDA); FY25 ₹136 cr. 2.5% of revenue from operations (including pass-through substrates) less intercompany sales; benchmarked by an independent third party and approved by the independent directors (CFO, Dec-2025). Because the base is revenue, the ~₹486 cr of substrates (no value added) cost ~₹12 cr of royalty a year. The group applied for a unilateral APA (FY24-28, rollback FY21-23) on royalty and management-support charges, then filed to withdraw it (AR FY26 consolidated note 45).

sections.title: Revenue grew 4% a year in FY23-26 but EBITDA 17%: the margin story is mix and pass-through, not volume

blocks.p: Reported revenue went from ₹4,827 cr in FY23 to ₹5,404 cr in FY26, only 4% a year, and fell 11% in FY25. That understates the business: revenue includes substrates (ceramic catalysts coated with platinum, palladium and rhodium) that Tenneco buys at the customer's direction and bills at cost. Substrates were ₹925-1,199 cr in FY23-24 and ~₹490-510 cr in FY25-26 (the company does not explain the drop; precious-metal prices and customer sourcing both move it). Value-added revenue (VAR, revenue less substrates) grew 8% a year, from ₹3,902 cr to ₹4,918 cr. EBITDA rose from ₹571 cr to ₹925 cr (17% a year): 14.6% of VAR in FY23, 18.8% in FY26. Net profit rose from ₹381 cr to ₹604 cr (₹624 cr before the FY26 labour-code charge).

sections.title: Clean audit, but three things to adjust for: pooled history, VAR, and the Motocare cash

bullets: **Pooled history.** The FY23-26 accounts combine four companies that came under one roof only in Mar-2025 (Ind AS 103 common-control pooling). They are fair for trends, but the businesses were run as sister companies, with their own transfer prices and dividends, for most of that period.

**VAR is a management measure.** It removes substrates from revenue. It is the right lens for margins, but it is not audited as a line item; we reconcile it to reported revenue every quarter (substrates = revenue less VAR, 6-12% of VAR).

**FY26 cash flow is flattered.** Operating cash of ₹1,429 cr includes ~₹663 cr of the Motocare sale consideration (an intra-group sale booked in Mar-2025), shown in "other working-capital items". Without it, cash from operations was ~₹766 cr, 83% of EBITDA; the company's own adjusted FCF/EBITDA is 58%.

**One-offs.** Q1FY26 profit included Motocare-related and other one-off income (size not disclosed; other income ₹31 cr that quarter); Q3FY26 carried a ₹27 cr labour-code charge (₹20 cr after tax). Our forecasts carry neither.

**Related-party charges** (2.6% of revenue) were restructured in the IPO year (network fees replaced management-support and corporate charges) and the transfer-pricing APA was withdrawn: watch the fee line.
**Minorities** are immaterial (~₹1 cr a year): net profit equals profit for EPS.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Deloitte audits the accounts and we found nothing improper. The amber reflects a short, reconstructed history, a non-GAAP headline metric and a cash-flow year inflated by an intra-group sale.

sections.title: No debt, negative working capital, ₹571 cr of cash at Mar-2026

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Tenneco India had no bank debt, ₹51 cr of lease liabilities and ₹571 cr of cash: net cash ₹520 cr. Working capital is negative (company: −8 days of net working capital excluding cash; cash-conversion cycle −23 days) because suppliers are paid in ~111 days while customers pay in ~43 and stock turns in ~35. Equity is small (₹1,198 cr) after ₹1,037 cr of pre-IPO dividends, which is why returns on equity (~43%) and capital look so high.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a market leader at 23.0x Sep-28E EPS; BUY, with a parent overhang

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading truck and off-highway exhaust supplier and car shock-absorber maker, net cash, negative working capital, with Tenneco's technology and an order book that covers FY28. Ride control (+27.9% in Q1FY27) is growing fast and is not hurt by EVs. You are also buying a company whose parent takes 2.6% of revenue in fees, owns most of its export customers and has sold 37% of the company in nine months.

**What you are paying:** 30.3x our FY27E and 25.0x FY28E EPS for ~17% a year EPS growth. Since listing the market has paid a median 29.0x forward; today it pays 25.0x, near the bottom of its 24.7-35.3x range, after the August block. The street's targets (median ₹667) are above ours because their EPS is higher.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Tenneco Clean Air India (consolidated; Rs crore). Two reported segments measured on value-added revenue (VAR = revenue less pass-through substrates): Clean Air & Powertrain Solutions (CA&PT) and Advanced Ride Technologies (ART). The engine models one revenue line; the segment build (CA&PT VAR + ART VAR + substrates = revenue) is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue in TENNIND.ctx.js. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Revenue = VAR + substrates. VAR: CA&PT +11% / +14% / +13% and ART +22% / +16% / +15% (lineBuild). FY27: Q1FY27 VAR +18.4% (CA&PT +9.6%, ART +27.9%) on the post-GST-cut PV boom; ART runs above 90% utilisation, so H2 growth slows against Q3-Q4FY26 bases that already grew 24-26%. FY28-29: the Rs12,400 cr lifetime order book covers more than 100% of the FY28 revenue target (company, Mar-2026); CAFE-3 (expected from 2027) and Kharkhoda (Clean Air, SoP ~Q3FY27) and the western ART plant lift CA&PT; DaVinci DCx and semi-active dampers keep ART ahead of PV production. Substrates (precious-metal coated, passed through at cost) held at ~11% of VAR (Q1FY27 11.8%, FY26 9.9%).

lineBuild._why: Company disclosure (Q4FY26 call, 3-Jun-2026): FY26 VAR Rs4,918 cr = CA&PT Rs2,430 cr + ART Rs2,489 cr; revenue from operations Rs5,404 cr, so substrates Rs486 cr. Forecast VAR by segment below; substrates are the balance to model revenue and must stay within 9-13% of VAR (ctx check).

assumptions._marginWhy: On revenue (Screener basis). FY26 17.1% of revenue = 18.8% of VAR (highest ever); Q1FY27 16.0% of revenue = 17.9% of VAR, down 170 bp YoY on non-indexed commodity costs (crude-linked rubber, plastics after the West Asia war), rupee weakness and the running cost of a listed company. Mix works against the margin: in FY25 CA&PT earned 23.8% of VAR and ART 12.8% (RHP via JM Financial), and ART is the faster-growing half (53-54% of VAR by FY28-29E vs 47% in FY25); at FY26 segment margins the mix alone takes ~0.2-0.3 points a year off. FY27E 18.0% of VAR: steel is indexed with a one-quarter lag and recoveries are under negotiation (CFO, Aug-2026). FY28-29E 18.6-18.8% of VAR as listing costs are absorbed (CFO, Dec-2025: margins 'come back to the same levels') and DCx/export mix helps (export margins 'in line or better'). Royalty (2.5% of revenue net of intercompany sales) and network service fees stay inside costs.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance Rs350-450 cr ('indicative', fully from internal accruals, Q1FY27 call), including Rs140 cr for the two announced plants (Kharkhoda Clean Air Rs71 cr; western India ART Rs69 cr). We take the low end because FY26 cash capex was only Rs115 cr and H1 spend had not been disclosed by 30-Sep. Rs280 cr a year in FY28-29 for semi-active suspension, CAFE-3/BS-VII hot ends and export-transfer lines.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs108 cr = 9.0% of average gross block (Rs1,195 cr; Screener schedules). Q1FY27 Rs28 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP flat), so 9% on a growing block front-loads depreciation.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening net cash (Mar-2026: cash Rs571 cr less Rs51 cr of lease liabilities = Rs520 cr). Bank deposits ~6.5%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury items (export incentives, scrap/asset-sale gains, interest on deposits with landlords). FY26 other income Rs59 cr before the Rs27 cr labour-code exceptional (AR FY26), but Q1FY26 carried a one-off from the Motocare disposal and other one-off income (CFO, Aug-2026; Q1FY26 Rs31 cr); the last three quarters ran at Rs9-12 cr a quarter before exceptional items. FY27E = Rs34 cr treasury + Rs6 cr = Rs40 cr, in line with the ~Rs37 cr TTM run rate.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 finance cost Rs34 cr (Q1FY27 Rs8 cr): lease interest plus interest on other items (AR FY26: Rs24 cr 'interest on others'); no bank debt.
assumptions._taxWhy: New regime 25.17% plus non-deductible items; FY25 24.5%, FY26 25.9% (incl. exceptional), Q1FY27 25%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: All FY26 dividends (Rs1,037 cr, Rs25.68 a share) were paid to Tenneco before the IPO (Apr-Aug 2025); the Board recommended no final dividend for FY26, citing capacity expansion, technology and 'other business opportunities' (AR FY26), and management talked of M&A options for surplus cash (Aug-2026). No interim declared by 30-Sep, so FY27E 0%; we assume a policy payout of 25-30% from FY28E (our assumption, not guidance).

dcf._betaWhy: Tied to Indian truck, tractor and car production (cyclical) but net cash and diversified across PV/CV/off-highway: beta 0.95, cost of equity 12.2%. No debt, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian vehicle production ~5-6% plus emission and ride content; but clean-air content disappears in battery EVs: 6%, the top of the house range only because ART is powertrain-agnostic.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~14% in FY29E to 8%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 16.5% of revenue (~18.3% of VAR): exhaust content shrinks as EV share rises.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~3.5% of revenue long run (FY23-26 1.2-2.1%, FY27E 5.5%); depreciation ~2.2% of revenue.
